core_obligations: Reduce to X affine using that an integral scheme has injective restriction maps on functions, then realize X as a nonempty open of a projective variety by taking the closure in projective space (proof lines 5253-5261).

Introduce the normalization of that projective variety and verify the three properties needed: it is finite and dominant with normal source, it is proper because properness is stable under finite morphisms and composition, and the normalization is surjective because its image is closed and contains the generic point (proof lines 5263-5278).
Conclude by applying the normal proper case to the inverse image of X under the normalization, since the unit groups and the quotients by k^* agree up to the identification (proof lines 5279-5282).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to X an open of a projective variety (proof lines 5253-5261).
Normalize and check finiteness, properness and surjectivity (proof lines 5263-5278).
Invoke the normal proper case (proof lines 5279-5282).
difficulty_reason: Over an algebraically closed field k, for an integral scheme X locally of finite type, the lemma shows that O^*(X)/k^* is a finitely generated abelian group (statement lines 5245-5250). The proof reduces the case at hand to the normal proper case by two moves that each need justification: since X is integral the restriction to a nonempty open is injective on functions, so one may assume X affine, and then X is realized as a nonempty open of a projective variety by taking the closure in projective space (proof lines 5253-5261). The normalization of that projective variety is finite, dominant and normal, and the author verifies that it stays a proper variety because properness is stable under finite morphisms and composition, and that it surjects onto the original variety because the image is closed and contains the generic point; since the inverse image of the affine open is then the scheme to which the previous normal case applies, the reduction is complete (proof lines 5263-5282). The claim is H2: the whole content is the reduction, with the previous normality lemma doing the actual counting.
